$comment: Phase-2 wave-1 OpenConnector ingestion config for Latvia IUB (Iepirkumu uzraudzības biroja, the Latvian Procurement Monitoring Bureau) - the W3 dead-tendril REVIVAL proof from README.md's audit table. concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_latvia_iub.py points at three now-dead/wrong endpoints in order (OPEN_DATA_API='https://open.iub.gov.lv/api/v1/notices', a CKAN search against data.gov.lv, and an /export/notices guess) - none of those were used here, per the task that produced this file: the W3 audit's revival path is the DAILY eForms-JSON bulk at open.iub.gov.lv/data, which is a completely different (correct, live) surface the old script never found. Discovery path, confirmed live 2026-07-05: GET /data returns an HTML (Symfony/Turbo) browse page, not JSON - it links to /data/notice, /data/xml (raw per-year eForms XML, 2013-2025) and /data/complaint; /data/notice drills down /data/notice/{year} -> /data/notice/{year}/{month} -> a list of per-day files literally named /data/notice/{year}/{month}/{DD-MM-YYYY}.json. Fetched /data/notice/2026/07/04-07-2026.json live: a plain JSON array (no envelope), 24 real eForms notices, ~290KB. This is genuine EU eForms structure (BT-* business terms - e.g. `identifier` is the notice's own UUID, `name`/BT-21 is the title, `organizationData` is the buyer party, `cpvType`/BT-262 the main CPV code), deeply nested for lot/contract/winner detail but with a stable, mostly-flat top-level envelope that a dot-notation mapping can reach. `noticeType` on that day's 24 records was entirely from the pil-/sps- (award-and-contract) notice family (pil-award x11, pil-contract x9, pil-concluded-contract, pil-planned-contract, pil-prior-information, sps-contract x1 each), including two pre-award stages within that family (pil-planned-contract, pil-prior-information carry `estimatedValue` with no `awardedValue` yet - confirmed live post-fix: one synced object shows `estimatedValue: "900000.00"`, `awardedValue: null`) - but no open call-for-tenders (cn-standard) notice was observed in this sample, so no confirmed field for a submission deadline exists yet; `closingDate` is deliberately left unmapped rather than guessing an eForms BT-131-shaped path that hasn't been seen live. Per-field presence was checked across all 24 records: `identifier`, `name`, `noticeType`, `cpvType`, `organizationData.name`, `organizationData.nutsCode`, `procurementProject.description` were present on 24/24 and are mapped as bare dot-paths; `tenderingProcess.procedureType` (23/24) and the `automaticallyCalculated.statementValue.*.sum` value fields (2-9/24, they vary by noticeType - award-stage notices carry `noticeContractValue`, pre-award ones would carry `estimatedValue`) are wrapped in `{{ x.y|default('') }}` per the mapping-engine gotcha below. `contractValue`/`currency`/`contractEnd`/`categorySlug` have no confirmed source field in this sample and are deliberately left unmapped rather than forced. Just like tenderned.json, this ingests the FULL daily feed with no IT/CPV filtering baked in (Specter's own `is_it_cpv()`/48-or-72-prefix check is the DB-side classification layer, not an API constraint) - confirmed live: 04-07-2026's 24 notices include CPV prefixes 79/45/50/39/33/37/77/15, i.e. none happen to be IT/software that day, which is expected variance for a full unfiltered feed, not a mapping bug. TWO mapping-engine design points worth flagging: (1) `publicationDate` and the Synchronization's `sourceConfig.endpoint` both use a self-contained Twig expression - `{{ 'now'|date_modify('-1 day')|date('Y-m-d') }}` for the value, `{{ 'now'|date_modify('-1 day')|date('Y') }}/{{ ... }}/{{ ... }}` for the path - that reads no source field at all (MappingService::executeMapping falls through to Twig whenever the mapping value isn't a literal dot-path found on the object, and the same holds for SynchronizationService's endpoint-templating whenever the string contains `{{ }}`; a bare Twig date expression always renders, object-independent). This is legitimate here (unlike inventing data) because the source's OWN URL structure encodes exactly one calendar day per file - every notice in a given day's file was dispatched that day by construction. Empirically confirmed inside the actual openconnector build (docker exec into the spectr-spike container, Twig::Environment + the real vendor/twig): `{{ 'now'|date_modify('-1 day')|date('d-m-Y') }}` on 2026-07-05 renders '04-07-2026', matching the real file fetched live. Practical upshot: unlike dutch_laws_bwb.json's BWB lawArticle sync (which needs an operator-supplied `data.xmlUrl` and therefore ships its Job disabled), this synchronization needs NO external `data` at invocation time - `sourceConfig.endpoint` computes 'yesterday' fresh on every scheduled tick, so the Job below ships genuinely enabled on a DAILY interval (86400s, not the wave-1 default weekly 604800s - deliberate, matches the source's own daily-bulk cadence). KNOWN LIMITATION: because each run only ever fetches 'yesterday', a job outage of N days silently skips those N days with no backfill (no maxPages-style multi-day walk is wired) - acceptable for the wave-1 single-day proof, worth a `sourceConfig.daysBack` knob before this is trusted for gap-free historical coverage. (2) `cpvCodes` cannot be built by combining `cpvType` (the single main code) with `additionalCpvType` (an array) the way the Python script does (`[cpv_main] + cpv_additional`), because MappingService's Twig fallback ALWAYS renders to a string (`{{ }}` output is fundamentally text, confirmed empirically - a Twig expression that evaluates to a PHP array just prints the word 'Array' with a PHP warning, verified live in the spectr-spike container) - Twig cannot be used to compute or return an array value, only the two structural mechanisms MappingService actually supports can: a bare dot-path taken verbatim from the source (already an array), or a literal static array/object written directly in the mapping JSON. Solved here using the THIRD, less obvious mechanism - the `cast` pipeline runs after mapping and applies PHP's own `(array)` cast, which turns a scalar into a single-element array - so `cpvCodes` is a bare dot-path to `cpvType` (the higher-value field: present 24/24 vs. additionalCpvType's 8/24) plus `"cast": {"cpvCodes": "array"}`, giving e.g. `["79212200-5"]` rather than an empty array. `additionalCpvType` is dropped from the array as a documented, deliberate simplification. This cast-to-array trick is written up as a new addition to IMPORT.md's mapping-engine gotcha section since it will be useful for any future source with the same 'one main code + one array of extras' shape. No sourceHashMapping is defined - no spurious daily-changing counter field was found in this source (unlike tenderned.json's aantalDagenTotSluitingsDatum), so the engine hashing the raw fetched object is fine. LIVE-VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-07-05 on the isolated spectr-spike instance (NC 34, OR 0.2.17-unstable.7, OC 0.2.16, spectr register id=8): imported clean via POST /apps/openregister/api/configurations/import (4 objects, no skipped entries), ran via POST /apps/openconnector/api/synchronizations/latvia-iub-to-spectr-tender/run with NO patching needed (unlike tenderned.json's maxPages workaround - this source is naturally one-file-per-run) - first run `found: 24, created: 24`, matching the 24 real notices independently confirmed in the raw daily file beforehand; only 1 HTTP request to open.iub.gov.lv (well inside the ≤8-request budget). Re-ran the same synchronization: `found: 24, updated: 24, created: 0` - same 24 target uuids reused (no duplicates), same originHash byte-identical before/after (same non-conclusive update-vs-skip engine behaviour tenderned.json already documents). Spot-checked across all 24 synced objects: 0 with a null/empty `displayName`, 0 literal-dot-path leaks on any Twig-wrapped field, `cpvCodes` genuinely typed `array` on every object (the cast-to-array trick holds up across the whole batch, not just one record), `publicationDate` uniformly '2026-07-04' (yesterday, matching the Twig date computation). ONE PRE-EXISTING ENVIRONMENT BUG FOUND AND FIXED, unrelated to this file's own correctness but blocking verification of it: the spike instance's live `spectr`/`tender` schema (id=9) was stale relative to this repo's register/spectr_register.json - it was missing the `displayName` property entirely (`configuration.objectNameField` was still `title`, `required` was still `[sourceRef,source,title]`), a drift from BEFORE `spectr_register.json` was 'extended with displayName for the objectNameField overlay' per that schema's own description. Confirmed via direct Postgres inspection of the magic table (`oc_openregister_table_8_9` had no `display_name` column at all) and via a plain direct-API object create (bypassing OpenConnector entirely) that also came back with `displayName: null` - proving this was a schema/environment gap, not a mapping or OpenConnector bug (tenderned.json's own existing live objects show the exact same null `displayName`, despite that file's $comment claiming a spot-checked `displayName` value - that claim did not hold up on re-inspection 2026-07-05, most likely checked before this schema drift, or before a container reset). Fixed by PATCH /apps/openregister/api/schemas/9 (with `acknowledgeBreaking: true`, since adding a required field without a default is classified as a breaking change) adding `displayName` to `properties`/`required` and setting `configuration.objectNameField` to `displayName` (kept the live schema's existing `objectDescriptionField: description` untouched, a minimal/additive patch rather than a full re-sync from the file) - OpenRegister's own `MagicMapper::ensureTableForRegisterSchema()`/`handleExistingTable()` self-healed the physical column (`display_name text`, plus a facet index) automatically on the very next object write, no manual `ALTER TABLE` needed. This was an environment-only fix (live schema state in the isolated spike instance), not a repository file change - worth re-applying (or re-importing spectr_register.json properly) if the spike instance is ever reset from an older snapshot.

objects.name: Latvia IUB Open Data
objects.description: Latvian Procurement Monitoring Bureau (Iepirkumu uzraudzības birojs) open-data eForms notice bulk. Public, unauthenticated, daily per-day JSON files. W3 revival (README.md audit): the old open.iub.gov.lv/api/v1/notices path is dead; this is the real, live, no-auth surface. Feeds the spectr `tender` register/schema via the latvia-iub-to-spectr-tender synchronization.

objects.name: Latvia IUB to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Maps a raw Latvia IUB eForms notice (one element of a /data/notice/{Y}/{M}/{DD-MM-YYYY}.json daily bulk array) onto the spectr `tender` schema. Field paths confirmed live 2026-07-05 against the real 04-07-2026 daily file (24 notices) - see this file's $comment for per-field presence rates and the two mapping-engine design points (self-contained 'yesterday' Twig dates, and the cast-to-array trick for cpvCodes).

objects.name: Latvia IUB to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Wave-1 ingestion sync: Latvia IUB's daily eForms bulk file for 'yesterday' (computed fresh on every run via a self-contained Twig date expression, no external `data` needed - see $comment) -> spectr register, tender schema. `resultsPosition: '_root'` because each daily file is a bare JSON array, no envelope (confirmed live). `usesPagination: false` - each day is its own single-file resource, there is no next-page concept within a day; date-axis coverage comes from the daily Job cadence below, not from OpenConnector's page counter.

objects.name: Latvia IUB Daily Sync
objects.description: Runs the latvia-iub-to-spectr-tender synchronization daily (86400s) - matches the source's own daily-bulk-file cadence, not the wave-1 default weekly interval used by the other sources in this directory. Genuinely unattended (unlike dutch_laws_bwb.json's disabled lawArticle Job): the endpoint needs no per-call `data`, it computes 'yesterday' itself on every tick.
